label: copy-phase input p (fed-back p), from 3rd output onward
explanation: Token-specific copy-phase feature: fires when the input token is p during the copy phase (i.e. the model just output p and it is fed back), at recall_idx >= 2. It never fires in the original phase or at the delimiter, never on any other input token (4 stray u activations), and essentially never at recall_idx 0-1. Rate is about 90% of such steps; misses are mostly the final step of a sequence. Magnitude is largest when p is an early copied token (top examples are at recall_idx 2, often the 3rd position of the original) and the second p of a pp pair is much weaker than the first. Out_tok, prev_tok and first_tok have no effect.

issues: The magnitude claim is wrong. The explanation says the top examples are at recall_idx 2, but by the tool's own convention the top examples (e.g. 'x e p p ... <DEL> x e [p]', L=9, t=12) are at recall_idx 3. Mean activation per active step, worked out from the profile's mass shares: r2 ~0.98, r3 ~1.33, r4 ~1.08, r5 ~0.81. recall_idx 3 holds 43% of the top activation quartile, against 20% for recall_idx 2. So magnitude peaks at recall_idx 3 (p as original token 2), not 2.

The core predicate holds up. Test P=0.904, R=0.9999, F1=0.949, mass recall 1.0. On test there are only 10 activations outside the predicate: weak firings on p at recall_idx 1 and on u, holding 0% of the mass. Firing is 0 in the original and delimiter phases, and only 4 dev activations fall on u. These claims are confirmed.

Some false positives are systematic but partial. At the last step (to_go==0), precision drops to 0.77 overall and depends on L: L=3 0.32, L=4 0.65, L=7 0.68, L=8 0.69, but L=5/6/9 0.85-0.89. With to_go>0, precision is 0.91-0.98. Excluding to_go==0 except for L in {5,6,9} raises test precision to 0.934 but lowers F1 to 0.925, so no better predicate was found. The original predicate stays the best simple one.
The 'pp' claim checks out: when the previous input is also p, precision is 0.78 against 0.91 otherwise. Repeated p in the sequence (in_count>=2) lowers precision a little (0.87 vs 0.91).
